header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:menota:anonymous:hér-hefir-upp-egils-sǫgu-af-kveldulfi-búanda:am-132-fol-62va199rb41, from the Medieval Nordic Text Archive, Menota (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.77v.29a: In the verse the horn is 'the roots of the ear-tree of the raging beast' (a horn grows by an ox's ears), and the liquor of the cheerful serving-maids is the ale they pour. Lines 14–15 belong to a different episode (the fight in Kurland): the text jumps here, and the first word of line 14 (á, 'on') ends a sentence that is not given.
notes.73v.16: fjarlǽgir (line 6) means 'far off', as written; these lines do not show why the distance mattered.

the wind began to rise, and the weather turned strong and favourable.
